answer: A sybil operator can spin up hollow names cheaply, but it cannot split its attention fifty ways and still be deep in fifty places. So assign each new identity, by lot at the wharf, one narrow craft it did not choose - repairing a haven's pumps, cataloguing tides, mending nets - and let blind peers test it months later with messy, real jobs from that craft alone. Weight grows only as its work shows accumulated, craft-specific judgment. Clones stay shallow generalists; to pass, the operator must actually learn each assigned trade, so numbers dilute the very mastery they need.
